transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Jared Miller (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (CTO, Cypher Labs), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng), Nina Park (Security), Marco Ruiz (ML Eng), Samir Patel (Product)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
Cypher is evaluating migration from OpenAI-hosted endpoints to a dedicated Redwood deployment. Key concerns: latency vs cost tradeoffs, vLLM/TGI compatibility, eval parity with current OpenAI models, SOC2/KMS/SSO requirements, and benchmark workflow. Redwood AE/SE to provide pricing, security docs, and run benchmark with customer's prompt set.

Topics:
- Current stack & pain points
- Performance / latency expectations
- Model compatibility (vLLM, TGI) and tokenization differences
- Security / compliance (SOC2, KMS, SSO, audit logs)
- Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC)
- Next steps / PoC plan

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Jared: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, this is Jared from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account, with me is Priya, our SE.
[00:00:08] Priya: hi all, thanks for making time. quick agenda


 hear about your current setup, constraints, and then talk through dedicated options and benchmarks.
[00:00:20] Aisha: thanks, Jared, Priya. I'll kick off. We're Cypher Labs, building a real-time code assistant inside IDEs; currently using OpenAI for completions and chat, and monthly spend is pretty high and latency is... hit-or-miss. We're evaluating Dedicated to get cost predictability and lower p95.
[00:00:40] Liam: yeah, we see tail latencies during peak hours; the KV cache behavior in the OpenAI flow isn't ideal for our prefix caching, and we lose context sometimes.
[00:00:50] Priya: when you say KV cache, do you mean your internal key-value cache for token embeddings or the model's kv cache?
[00:00:55] Liam: model's KV cache


 like repeated prompts that share prefix, we'd like faster reuse, less token re-encoding, that sort of thing.
[00:01:04] Marco: also curious about compatibility


 we're prototyping some local inference with vLLM and TGI, and want to know if the same prompts/evals give parity when moved to Redwood Dedicated.
[00:01:15] Priya: totally. a couple notes up front: Redwood's runtime supports standard model formats, and we have verified performance profiles for the common open models. vLLM/TGI clients typically interface differently; we do compatibility testing, but there can be tokenization and sampling differences.
[00:01:32] Samir: can you explain sampling differences


 like would temperature or top_p produce different completions?
[00:01:36] Priya: yes, slightly. sampling RNG and tokenization can differ; but in our experience eval-level parity is achievable with prompt tuning and a short calibration run. we'll run side-by-side evals.
[00:01:48] Aisha: our success criteria are 1) p95 latency <= 300ms for small completions, 2) cost reduction ~40% or better, 3) no regression in our eval suite (we have ~1k prompts).
[00:02:00] Jared: good, that's helpful. to confirm: is data residency or KMS a hard requirement?
[00:02:06] Nina: yes


 we need customer-managed keys (KMS) and logs stored in our EU region for now. SOC2 is required; also SSO with SAML.
[00:02:16] Jared: okay, Dedicated with a private VPC can meet that; we have KMS integrations and audit logs. i'll share the SOC2 package and KMS guides after the call.
[00:02:28] Liam: what's the difference operationally between Dedicated and Private? we considered on-prem too.
[00:02:33] Priya: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools we host in customer-dedicated tenancy


 predictable throughput and SLA-backed latency. Private (VPC/on-prem) is for customers who need their own network or air-gapped requirements. On-prem is more involved. for your needs it sounds like Dedicated in an EU region with customer KMS would fit.
[00:02:53] Marco: performance question


 how do you handle batching and latency SLOs? our traffic is spiky.
[00:02:58] Priya: we use continuous batching with workload-aware policies and dynamic batching windows. you can configure SLOs


 if you prioritize latency we can tune for smaller batch sizes and more instances; if cost matters we suggest larger batch windows and prefix/KV caching.
[00:03:14] Aisha: can you talk about kernel selection and quantization? we're looking at int8 quant for cost savings.
[00:03:19] Priya: yes


 the runtime selects kernels based on model arch and seq length; quantization profiles are supported, and we recommend a quality vs cost sweep. some model variants degrade with aggressive quant, so we test on your eval set.
[00:03:33] Samir: any surprises when moving from OpenAI? prompt engineering changes?
[00:03:37] Priya: minor prompt tweaks sometimes


 tokenization differences can cause shifts. we typically run an eval parity pass to identify prompts that need canonicalization.
[00:03:46] Liam: about vLLM/TGI


 if we have a local vLLM pipeline, can we bring the same model to Redwood Dedicated?
[00:03:52] Priya: generally yes if it's a supported model format (HF, GGUF, etc.). TGI and vLLM clients talk differently to the runtime; we provide adapters and sample scripts. point is: runtime-level behavior can differ in corner cases


 we'll include compatibility notes in the bench harness.
[00:04:07] Marco: benchmarks


 what's realistic to expect for throughput?
[00:04:11] Priya: depends on model size and sequence length. for 13B models you can expect X tokens/sec on a T4 vs Y on an A100, but we'll put concrete numbers in the benchmark run.
[00:04:22] Aisha: ok, when you say X and Y, can we get a spreadsheet showing cost per 1M tokens across configurations?
[00:04:28] Jared: yes, i'll include a TCO spreadsheet comparing Hosted vs Dedicated reserved capacity and burst costs.
[00:04:35] Nina: security: do you support customer-managed HSM or just cloud KMS? also audit log retention timeline?
[00:04:42] Priya: we integrate with common cloud KMS and can support customer-managed keys; HSM is supported via enterprise channel. audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM, retention configurable. i'll include the security whitepaper.
[00:04:58] Aisha: what about model rollouts and canarying


 we need to be able to test new model versions without impacting prod.
[00:05:06] Priya: built-in rollout controls: canary deploys, A/B experiments, automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant if latency or error spikes. you can pin model versions per-route.
[00:05:18] Marco: do you track token-level latency and cost per route?
[00:05:21] Priya: yes


 Console shows token-level cost and latency breakdowns; tracing hooks and per-route dashboards.
[00:05:28] Samir: about support SLAs


 what's included in Dedicated?
[00:05:32] Jared: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime/latency tiers and a named CSM at higher tiers; enterprise support options exist for Private deployments. i'll outline tiers in the pricing doc.
[00:05:42] Aisha: timeline


 we want to be live in prod in Q2 if numbers check out. is that feasible?
[00:05:48] Jared: feasible, yes. typical flow: discovery -> benchmark PoC (2-3 weeks) -> pilot (1 month) -> prod. with a reserved capacity commit we can accelerate.
[00:06:00] Liam: we need to test parity for our eval suite; can Redwood run the eval side-by-side with OpenAI and with our vLLM runs?
[00:06:06] Priya: yes, we can run side-by-side evals. ideally you provide the prompt set, metrics, and acceptance thresholds. we'll run baseline on your OpenAI config and compare.
[00:06:17] Aisha: what's the expected delta usually? we've seen small differences but not more than a few percent.
[00:06:21] Priya: typically <5% accuracy delta after some prompt adjustments, sometimes 0% when model and sampling are aligned. quantization can widen that


 we'll test quant profiles.
[00:06:33] Marco: any gotchas for streaming vs non-streaming responses? some of our UX relies on streaming chunk-by-chunk.
[00:06:39] Priya: streaming is supported; for low-latency UX we recommend smaller max tokens and prefix caching. streaming semantics are consistent with OpenAI-compatible APIs, but again tokenization can shift chunk boundaries.
[00:06:53] Samir: procurement/contract questions


 do you have a standard enterprise agreement?
[00:06:57] Jared: yes, we have templates; procurement/legal review is usually the final step. for Dedicated we do a subscription/reservation contract.
[00:07:05] Nina: data deletion policies? retention?
[00:07:08] Priya: we support configurable retention and can avoid storing prompts if required; we'll document that in the security pack.
[00:07:14] Aisha: great. i want to dig into the benchmark specifics. Priya, can you outline what you'd need from us?
[00:07:20] Priya: we'll need: 1) prompt set (preferably JSONL), 2) traffic shape (p95/p50, concurrency), 3) model(s) you're using on OpenAI and any local vLLM configs, 4) metrics you care about (latency percentiles, token cost, correctness/accuracy). we'll provide harness scripts that run across OpenAI and Redwood endpoints for apples-to-apples.
[00:07:40] Liam: for vLLM compatibility, we currently use a patched vllm binary and TGI for GPU pooling. will that translate?
[00:07:46] Priya: likely yes, but we'll need to validate. please include config snippets; we'll run a quick compatibility check.
[00:07:53] Marco: can the benchmark include quantized runs?
[00:07:55] Priya: yes, we can run int8/4 quant tests as long as the model variant supports it. we'll show quality/cost tradeoff curves.
[00:08:03] Aisha: ok, rolling to next steps then. Jared, what will you send?
[00:08:07] Jared: i'll send the pricing/TCO spreadsheet and a short onboarding checklist. Priya will send the benchmark harness and sample scripts. i'll also share SOC2 and security docs.
[00:08:16] Nina: please include details on KMS/HSM and audit log retention and where logs can be shipped.
[00:08:21] Priya: will do.
[00:08:24] Samir: one last question


 if we find a regression in our evals, what's the remediation path?
[00:08:28] Priya: we have rollback and fallback policies: immediate rollback to previous model, canary isolation, and remediation with model tuning/quant config. we'll also attach regression alerts to the eval set.
[00:08:39] Aisha: perfect. thanks, everyone.
[00:08:42] Jared: great, thanks all. we'll follow up with docs and schedule the benchmark run


 suggested window next week.
[00:08:48] Priya: thanks, bye.

(automated transcript ends; remaining ~34 minutes were Q&A and detailed security/ops clarifications, snippets omitted for brevity)
